Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Young woman with acute onset dysuria, frequency/urgency, suprapubic aching worse with urination, and one episode of pink urine. No systemic or upper tract symptoms. Sexually active without barrier protection; on combined OCP; LMP 2 weeks ago.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):
  - Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis—High likelihood: classic lower urinary tract symptoms with possible hematuria; absence of fever/flank pain.
  - Urethritis due to STI (Chlamydia/Gonorrhoea)—Moderate likelihood: sexually active without condoms; dysuria can occur without discharge; less typical hematuria.
  - Urolithiasis—Low likelihood: hematuria possible, but no colicky flank pain or radiation; symptoms favor cystitis.
- Working diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis with possible hematuria.
- Management priorities: Start appropriate short-course antibiotic, obtain urine dipstick and culture, hydration, analgesia, safety-netting for red flags; follow-up if no improvement.

Management Plan

- Actions/treatments:
  - Antibiotic therapy: Trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin discussed as a 3-day course; start antibiotics (specific agent and dosing not documented).
  - Urine testing: Arrange urine sample drop-off for dipstick and culture; clinic to inform patient of results and sensitivities.
  - Symptomatic care: Encourage oral hydration; Paracetamol for pain as needed.
- Safety net:
  - Seek care urgently if fever, back/flank pain, or vomiting develop.
  - Return if symptoms persist or worsen by next week for reassessment.
- Counseling:
  - Advised to avoid cannabis use going forward. Alcohol use kept to social/moderate levels discussed.
- Follow-up:
  - Clinic will contact with urine result; patient to return if not improving.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

- Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis—High: Dysuria, frequency, suprapubic aching worse with urination; pink urine consistent with hematuria; no systemic or upper tract signs.
- Urethritis due to STI (Chlamydia/Gonorrhoea)—Moderate: Sexually active without condoms; dysuria can occur without discharge, though hematuria is less typical.
- Urolithiasis—Low: Pink urine could indicate hematuria, but absence of colicky flank pain and typical cystitis symptoms make this less likely.
